clue.text: Child received a bit of discipline in person

indicators.note: whoever receives something takes it in, so the child's word holds the single letter inside it

parts.note: a male child
the opening letter of discipline

explanation.surface: A youngster gets a taste of punishment face to face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In person' reads as one phrase, but 'in' only links the wordplay to the definition, person.
explanation.definitionFit: Body is an informal word for a human being, as in 'a nosy old body'.

clue.text: Nightclub employee is a lightweight in bedroom

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so the weight goes within the room's short form

parts.note: BR is the abbreviation for bedroom used in property listings
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A doorman at a club turns out to be a slight figure caught in someone's bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouncer is the doorman hired by a nightclub to keep out or remove troublemakers.

clue.text: Play dice, at first, with God

indicators.note: what comes at first is the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of dice
Rama is a Hindu god, an avatar of Vishnu

explanation.surface: An invitation to gamble with the Almighty, echoing Einstein's line that God does not play dice.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play written for the stage, so the noun stands for the answer.

clue.text: Faculty member with sampling of investment chart is bringing in 21

parts.note: a prof is a professor, a university teacher

indicators.note: a sampling is a small taste, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of investment
a table is a chart of figures

explanation.surface: An academic, armed with a slice of a portfolio graph, is earning a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 points to 21-down, whose answer is WEALTH, so the definition reads 'bringing in wealth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something profitable yields money, so 'bringing in wealth' describes it as an adjective phrase.

clue.text: Wobbly boxer

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the fighter played by Sylvester Stallone in the film series

explanation.surface: A prizefighter unsteady on his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocky means unstable or shaky, and Rocky Balboa is the fictional heavyweight from the Stallone films.

clue.text: What you might use to move slowly in terror, while eating fried grits

definitions.text: What you might use to move slowly

indicators.note: something eating another takes it inside, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: fear is a synonym for terror

indicators.note: frying turns food over and breaks it up, so the letters of the next word are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written; grits is a Southern US dish of ground corn

explanation.surface: Someone creeping along in fright while chewing on a plate of fried grits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In terror' looks like a phrase; 'in' belongs to the definition (what you use to move slowly in), and 'terror' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: First gear is the lowest gear of a car, the one used when driving at a crawl.

clue.text: Sweet stuff from Electra, after tragic development

indicators.note: a development changes something's form, so the name's letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written: the heroine of Greek tragedy

explanation.surface: Something saccharine emerges from the story of Electra once the tragedy unfolds.
explanation.walkthrough: Electra is the title figure of Greek tragedies by Sophocles and Euripides, which makes 'tragic' fit the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is the British name for molasses or golden syrup, and figuratively for cloying sentiment.

clue.text: Meddler, though, can slide downhill

parts.note: but and though both introduce a contrast
a tin is a can
to ski is to slide down a slope

explanation.surface: A busybody, though, may come sliding down a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual spelling ends in Y; the wordplay here builds the variant ending in I.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttinski is slang for someone who butts in on other people's business.

clue.text: They get a paycheck from leaderless students

indicators.note: without a leader means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: learners are students

explanation.surface: Wages handed out by a class with no one in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Earners are people paid for work, those who receive a regular wage.

clue.text: Plan with Lucy's husband on the outskirts of Galveston

parts.note: Desi Arnaz, Lucille Ball's husband on and off screen in I Love Lucy

indicators.note: a place's outskirts are its edges, so only the first and last letters count

parts.note: the edge letters of the Texas city

explanation.surface: A scheme hatched with Lucy's man on the edge of a Texas port.
explanation.walkthrough: I Love Lucy was a 1950s American sitcom starring Lucille Ball and her husband Desi Arnaz.
explanation.definitionFit: A design is a plan or scheme, as in 'by design'.

clue.text: Consumption in American century?

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States
an age is a long period, loosely a century

explanation.surface: A question about spending habits in the so-called American Century.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the amount of something used up, as in water or fuel usage.

clue.text: President assuming prison will produce someone helpful in assembling a cabinet

definitions.text: someone helpful in assembling a cabinet

indicators.note: to assume is to take on, so the leader's name takes the jail inside it

parts.note: Jimmy Carter, US president 1977-81
pen is US slang for a penitentiary

explanation.surface: A president behind bars somehow ends up helping form a government cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: Cabinet is the trick: the surface means a group of ministers, but the definition means a cupboard, which a woodworker builds.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter is a woodworker who builds furniture such as a cupboard.

clue.text: Organization to help the needy? Burn it before day's end

parts.note: to char is to scorch
taken as written

indicators.note: a word's end is its final letter alone

parts.note: the closing letter of day

explanation.surface: A cynical suggestion: torch the relief agency before the day is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A charity is a body set up to give aid to people in need.

clue.text: Without a tail, the best cat recoils, getting touchy?

indicators.note: to recoil is to spring back, so the combined letters are read backwards
something without a tail has lost its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: the elite are the best of a group
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prize cat missing its tail flinches when anyone comes near it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that touchy is taken literally, to do with touch, not irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactile means relating to the sense of touch, a playful reading of touchy.

clue.text: Note: central banks breaking up, intended to get another loan

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: something breaking up a word splits it apart and sits inside it

parts.note: a fiance is one's intended spouse

indicators.note: the central part of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: the middle letter of banks

explanation.surface: A memo: the big banks are breaking up, and what was intended was a second loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central banks' looks like a financial institution, which suits the loan theme, but it only supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To refinance is to replace an existing loan with a new one.

clue.text: Farm's ironclad right to vote

indicators.note: to be clad is to be wrapped or covered, so the metal surrounds the rest

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a ranch is a farm, and the 's stands for is
the printed word, read as iron followed by clad

explanation.surface: A farmer's unshakeable claim to a ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ironclad' reads as one word meaning firm, but splits into iron and clad.
explanation.definitionFit: The franchise is the right to vote in public elections, as in universal franchise.

clue.text: Sudden flood of French-German river's operating in a northbound direction

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading north means reading from the bottom up

parts.note: de is French for of
the Elbe flows through Germany; the 's adds S
a machine that is operating is on

explanation.surface: A flash flood on a river crossing the French-German border, running north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French-German river' suggests the Rhine; the hyphen hides a split between 'of French' and 'German river'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosebleed is a sudden flow of blood from the nose, wittily called a flood.

clue.text: Moderates rents after the first

indicators.note: keeping only what comes after the first letter means that letter is dropped

parts.note: to lease is to rent

explanation.surface: A landlord lowers rents once the opening month is past.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease something is to moderate or lessen it, as with pain or pressure.

clue.text: Celebrate breakfast with eggs, initially

indicators.note: a letter that breaks into a word splits it and sits inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of eggs
the printed word, read as break followed by fast

explanation.surface: Mark a special day with a morning meal of eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: Breakfast must be read as two words, break and fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To feast is to celebrate with a large meal.

clue.text: Punishers nabbing last of record-keepers?

indicators.note: to nab is to grab hold of, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: those who fine people punish them

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the closing letter of record

explanation.surface: Disciplinarians collaring the last of the archivists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record-keepers' looks like one compound; it splits so 'keepers?' alone is the definition, from the saying 'finders keepers'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the playground saying 'finders keepers', whoever finds a thing gets to keep it.

clue.text: Mexican city substituting piece of tin for damage in pot

indicators.note: substituting one thing for another swaps it into its place
a piece is a small part, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of tin
to mar is to damage
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A border town where a tin piece replaces the damaged bit in a cooking pot.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pot is a cooking vessel; here it means the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Tijuana is a large Mexican border city just south of San Diego.

clue.text: Writing carelessly about stomach heave

indicators.note: about means around, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: to sling is to throw or heave
a craw is a bird's crop, loosely a stomach

explanation.surface: Scribbling about a queasy stomach and retching.
explanation.walkthrough: Stomach and heave suggest nausea, but they give two plain nouns-and-verbs, the throw wrapped around the gut.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrawling is untidy, hasty handwriting.

clue.text: Break the law to make money

indicators.note: breaking something smashes it apart, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Crime pays: commit an offence and get rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealth means riches, a large store of money and possessions.

clue.text: Mischievous creature's smile involving slippery elm

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a grin is a broad smile

indicators.note: something slippery will not hold its shape, so the letters slide into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An imp grinning in the bark of a slippery elm, a real American tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary imp blamed for mechanical faults.

clue.text: Congratulatory message from a long-suffering inhabitant of the French Riviera?

parts.note: Nice is the chief city of the French Riviera, here describing where the man lives
Job is the Bible's byword for patient suffering

explanation.surface: A cheery note of praise from a patient sufferer living in Nice.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is read two ways: praise for good work, and a Job who lives in Nice.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Nice job' is an informal phrase of praise for something done well.

clue.text: Take up residence outside a city

indicators.note: one word outside another wraps around it

parts.note: to settle is to make a home somewhere
taken as written

explanation.surface: Moving to the suburbs beyond a big town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A city' looks like a single unit, but 'a' is wordplay and 'city' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is the largest city in Washington State, in the US Pacific Northwest.

clue.text: Mensch wants content that is not stressed

definitions.note: a clause describing the answer, a vowel that is not stressed

indicators.note: the contents of a phrase are what lies inside it, across its word break

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A good person wants a calm life without stress.
explanation.walkthrough: Mensch is Yiddish for a decent, honourable person; it supplies letters only.
explanation.definitionFit: A schwa is the neutral vowel heard in unstressed syllables, like the a in about.

clue.text: Contrarian entrepreneur's beginning to run business

indicators.note: a contrarian goes the opposite way, so the combined letters are read backwards
a word's beginning is its first letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of entrepreneur
to dart is to run quickly

explanation.surface: A maverick entrepreneur starting out to run a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade means commerce, the buying and selling that makes up business.

clue.text: Bite hazelnuts for queen

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the printed word, read as hazel followed by nuts

explanation.surface: Cracking hazelnuts as a treat for the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Hazelnuts must be split into hazel and nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth is the name of two English queens, most recently Elizabeth II.

clue.text: Footpath starting to turn in front of fence

indicators.note: where something starts is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of turn
a rail is a simple fence

explanation.surface: A walkway that begins to bend just ahead of a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail is a rough path, especially through countryside.

clue.text: River that female boatbuilder's embracing, also

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: Noah built the ark
and adds something, as also does

explanation.surface: A river that a woman shipwright is hugging too.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shenandoah is a river in Virginia and West Virginia, a tributary of the Potomac.

clue.text: Norm is not nice

explanation.surface: Someone called Norm turns out to be unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: The mean is the average of a set of values, and mean also describes spiteful behaviour.
